answer: Each agent ID has to post a bond of 50 tokens. That bond is locked for 30 days, and it gets slashed if two other bonded peers flag the ID for replaying the same task outputs. Cloning a thousand IDs therefore means locking up 50,000 tokens. A shared signal like identical latency, or the same timber price feed scraped from one shale-region endpoint, ties those clones together. Once one of them is caught, the others are exposed too, and the attacker loses every bond in the cluster.
